title: Helix Drop
observed_goal: The page text and the official goal card describe dropping the bouncing ball through the tower gaps all the way down; in the active-game frames, the ball, spiral tiers, and gaps are visible, but reaching the end was not observed.
observed_controls: It introduces the A and D keys for rotation; the page text also gives the left and right arrow keys and Drag for Spin.
Space is introduced in the page text for Start / retry and Esc for Pause.
In the active page, the instruction text Hold ◀ ▶ or drag sideways to spin is visible; definite acceptance of any input cannot be established from these frames.
observed_core_loop: In the active frames, a ball is positioned on/between ring-shaped tiers around a central axis, and the tier arrangement changes between frames; frame 04 shows particles and separated pieces and a score of 10. This evidence is a direct indication of active gameplay, but the complete repeated cycle of rotating, falling, passing through a gap, and continuing or failing was not fully observed in the frames.
progress_feedback: The active frames show Stage 1/6. The score is 0 in the after_start and after_key_burst frames and is shown as 10 in after_combined_input and late; a vertical bar is also visible on the right side of the active frames. Which input or event exactly caused this change was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
decisions_risk_reward: The page text and frames present decision-making about rotating the structure to align a gap with the ball’s path; the frames show continuous layers and a red section. Timing, collision risk, and the optimal choice between paths were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive in the recorded run; a change between two frames alone does not prove accepted input.
rewards: A numeric score of 0 and then 10 is visible in the active-frame HUD. The official card claims Smash through layers and dodge the red, but this claim was not confirmed by complete play or a final outcome in this recording.
penalties_failure: There is no direct frame of a loss, halt, definite collision, score decrease, or failure screen; the penalty status and failure condition were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive. The red section is visible in the frames only as a visual element, and its effect is not established by this evidence.
outcomes_replay: The page text introduces Space for Start / retry and Esc for Pause. A final outcome, win, loss, actual retry, or replay capability was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive in the frames.
onboarding: The load frame shows the title, a textual goal explanation, the Daily Tower, Random Practice, Leaderboard, and Settings options, and the input guide. The post-start frame changes to Stage 1/6 and a rotation guide. A step-by-step explanation of obstacles or a separate interactive tutorial was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
visual_audio_accessibility: The frames show a 3D scene with a central axis, gold/purple ring-shaped tiers, a bright ball, particles, and a dark background; large HUD text and a pause button are also visible. Audio cannot be assessed from the frames; the console records the presence of an AudioContext warning. Contrast, screen reader, full touch controls, and other accessibility conditions were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
technical_clues: A canvas with dimensions 1280×800 is recorded in the metadata; this is only a technical clue about the rendering surface, not proof of game logic.
Three scripts, one stylesheet, three fonts, and three fetches are recorded in the metadata; script contents were not scanned, and no engine marker or tuning constant candidate was recorded.
A fallback to software WebGL warning was recorded; this is a technical clue about the rendering environment and does not establish game behavior.

An AudioContext warning and a 403 error, along with failed/aborted leaderboard requests, are recorded in the metadata; their cause and effect on the game experience were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
The metadata explicitly states that visual change may be caused by animation or the passage of time and does not prove that inputs were understood.
transferable_principles: A one-sentence goal and low-density HUD can make the relationship among position, progress, and score quickly understandable.
Decision-making based on aligning a path with gaps can provide a simple skill-testing core without requiring a lengthy explanation.
Numeric and stage-based feedback should be distinct from merely decorative cues so that progress remains legible.
To draw conclusions about controls, a repeatable cycle and a direct outcome must be recorded; a change between two frames alone is insufficient.
candle_climber_relevance: For Candle Climber, a legible goal and stage-based feedback can serve as inspiration, but score/rank should reflect skill only.
No purchase- or wallet-based advantage for progression or scoring is recommended.

Any idea resembling a free brake, horizontal direction change, or branching path requiring a new control should be discarded; if examined, it should be presented only as a hypothesis requiring control and legibility testing, not as a conclusion from this game.
do_not_copy: Do not reproduce this game’s name, character, art style, color scheme, text, sound, brand, or assets.
Do not copy the card’s claim about a daily tower, breaking layers, or avoiding the red element as confirmed behavior; these were not completed in this playtest recording.
Avoid inferring accepted controls or scoring logic solely from changes between frames.
Do not treat the absence of an element in the load frame as its absence from the entire game.

evidence.claim: The load page describes dropping the bouncing ball through gaps and controlling rotation.
The official card describes the goal as Spin the tower and drop the bouncing ball through the gaps, all the way down.
In the active-game frame Stage 1/6, score 0, the ball, ring-shaped tiers, and a pause button are visible.
The active guide Hold ◀ ▶ or drag sideways to spin is visible in the stage text.
The after_key_burst frame still shows Stage 1/6 and score 0; input acceptance is not established by this change/lack of change.
The after_combined_input frame shows score 10, separated pieces/particles, and a red section at the bottom of the scene.
The late frame still shows Stage 1/6 and score 10, and the ball/motion effect is visible in the scene; the final outcome is not seen.
The visual change may be caused by animation or the passage of time and is not proof that the input was understood.
A canvas with dimensions 1280×800 and a software WebGL fallback are recorded in the metadata.

limitations: This analysis uses only evidence.json and five frames with the stages load, after_start, after_key_burst, after_combined_input, and late; no web browsing, replay, code reading, or hidden-control testing was performed. The recording reached active gameplay, but the complete repeated cycle, win/loss, actual retry, definite effect of each input, audio, and full accessibility were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive. The official card claim is reported separately from direct observation.
